projects.description:

By the end of the year, three meetings on  the scope of the FEEDCities in Azerbaijan, area of implementation and contractual  details were held. The objectives of the FEEDCities research are:

2. To assess the nutritional composition of the ready-to-eat foods sold in the street.
3. To map the spatial distribution of food advertisements and to describe the typology and contents of food advertisements.   
2) Expert team composed of WHO national and international experts, as well as representatives from Republican Hygiene and Epidemiology Center (HEC) visited selected Hygiene and Epidemiology Centers (HEC) in Sabunchu, Sabail, Ganja, Masalli, Astara districts, . The visits aimed to assess institutional capacities of these HECs in delivering essential public health functions and to identify the structural and functional refinements needed for better contribution to public health in Azerbaijan.
 During the visit experts conducted unstructured interviews with directors of HECs and public health workers, The information collected was used to produce a report with key recommendations for reform to the Ministry of Health. 
3)The World Health Organization (WHO) organized a meeting in Azerbaijan, with representatives from key health agencies to create a shared understanding of strengthening the country's public health system. Participants represented MoH, SAMHI, TABİB, the Food Safety Agency, The State Customs Committee, Public Health and Reforms Center, Azerbaijan Medical University, Ministry of Emergency Situations, and the Azerbaijan State Advanced Training Institute for Doctors. During the meeting, participants identified their institution’s role in delivering essential public health services and agreed on the need for having a platform to strengthen collaboration in addressing main public health challenges. 
Participants agreed to expand the group to include the Ministry of Ecology, Ministry of Labour and Social Protection, State Committee for Family, Women and Children and Health Committee of the Parliament. The idea of a Public Health Symposium, involving national and international partners, was explored to raise awareness and discuss global health trends, fostering enhanced cooperation.

projects.name: 2.1.2.36 - Strengthen emergency medical care services
projects.description:
Over a recent period, a comprehensive effort was made to enhance the capacity and knowledge of healthcare professionals in Azerbaijan, focusing on emergency care systems (ECS), through various educational initiatives and collaborations.

The initiatives began with a three-day ECS Training course on Basic Life Support (BLS) and Advanced Cardiac Life Support (ACLS) Train-the-Trainer (ToT) for 19 health workers from emergency units. This was followed by a capacity group study visit to Turkish universities, where participants gained firsthand experience in emergency care system organization, case management, and emergency unit design. A significant number of healthcare education professionals, 152 from ASATID and AMU, attended ToT sessions in January and February, highlighting the commitment to training educators in these critical areas.

A pivotal development was the completion of the HEAT assessment at eight project hospitals, leading to a final report that underscores the ongoing evaluation and improvement efforts in healthcare facilities. Concurrently, a “ECS Workshop for Curriculum Development” was held, attracting 68 representatives and culminating in a comprehensive report that outlined the curriculum development process for medical education in Azerbaijan, with plans for further development of educational materials.

Further, the ECS Capacity Group Study Visit to Türkiye marked another collaborative effort under the Health Professionals’ Education focus area, signifying international cooperation. Throughout a three-month period, 266 participants completed BLS and ACLS training programs at SUM-Sim, demonstrating a broad engagement with the training programs. Specialized training, such as the PHTLS Training Program, was also conducted for emergency care doctors and candidate trainers, enhancing the specialized skills required for emergency care.

ECS Webinar sessions played a crucial role in reaching out to a wider audience, with 550 participants in the initial sessions and a total of 1170 participants in subsequent series, highlighting the scalability of digital learning platforms. Community engagement was also a priority, as evidenced by CPR Awareness Community Events and Training, which educated over 300 people in CPR skills, and a first aid awareness training session for UNDP Baku office employees.

The summer period saw 257 physicians from TABIB successfully completing BLS and ACLS training courses at SUM-Sim, indicating the training's appeal to medical professionals. The academic landscape was further enriched with the launch of the Department of Emergency Medicine and the implementation of instructional materials for the 4th year Emergency Medicine clerkship, developed by WHO experts.

Additional ToT training courses in PHTLS and BLS & ACLS were conducted, reaching more participants and extending the training's impact. The procurement of BLS and ACLS mannequins and the advancement of medical devices and equipment procurement demonstrate the logistical support backing these educational endeavors.

This narrative chronicles a multi-faceted approach to improving emergency care education and capacity in Azerbaijan, featuring international collaboration, comprehensive training programs, and significant community engagement efforts. WHO Azerbaijan CO held a community engagement demonstration to promote and raise awareness of the importance of learning cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) skills among the guests of the high-level regional meeting of WHO/Europe and local health authorities (MOH, TABIB, SAMHI) on the "Fit-For-Purpose Hospitals" event on 6 June. Guests included around 200 government representatives, hospital practitioners, and partners from across the WHO European Region Guests. CPR is a vital first response during sudden cardiac arrest. It is not necessary to be a medical professional to perform CPR; anyone can learn these skills. The participants had a chance to learn about and practice CPR on the special mannequin under the supervision of our doctors during the event.

projects.name: 2.1.2.32 - Support to enhance national capacity on vaccination
projects.description:
1) To support Azerbaijan’s government efforts on ensuring the successful uptake of routine childhood vaccination, series of training for HCWs were organized in four regions of Azerbaijan (Goygol, Yevlakh, Minghechevir, Gobustan) that are the regions with lowest vaccination among under 6 years old children together with UNICEF and in collaboration with MoH, TABIB, SAMHI, and regional executive power offices. The main goal of the training was to enhance the skills of healthcare workers in those regions based on best practice guidelines for routine immunization.  During the event, 136 PHC workers were trained.
Stakeholders: MoH, TABIB, SAMHI, UNICEF

2) The interactive events aimed to build trust and demand for vaccines among parents, by providing them with accurate information about vaccines and dispelling myths and misconceptions about their safety and efficacy. 

As part of the campaign, 500 families with children who missed their routine immunizations have been personally invited to the meeting with trusted health-care professionals. In a single day of activities, about 70% of the un- and under-immunized children received their vaccines while nearly 80% of attending parents had initially delayed or declined vaccination of these children. 
Stakeholders: MoH, TABIB, SAMHI, UNICEF
Beneficieries: population, parents

3) WHO, the Azerbaijan Pediatric Society (AzPC), and TABIB conducted trainings on October 27 and November 17 in Shirvan and Lankaran cities, respectively. 
This event was dedicated to underscoring the significance of child vaccination. A series of events organized in the regions, titled "Embracing Scientific Evidence Over Myths: Vaccination Awareness Training," was held under the motto "Leave no one behind" in accordance with the WHO's European Immunization Agenda 2030. The primary goal of the training was to enhance the skills of healthcare workers in those regions based on best practice guidelines for routine immunization. 
The event involved 132 pediatricians and nurses from Shirvan and 76 healthcare workers from Lankaran and surrounding cities.
Stakeholders: MoH, TABIB, AzPc 

4) To raise awareness on vaccination, WHO, the Azerbaijan Pediatric Society (AzPC), and TABIB conducted awareness-raising events on October 27 and November 17 in Shirvan and Lankaran cities, respectively. During the events, Board Members of AzPC and experts from the Ministry of Health engaged in discussions with parents on vaccine hesitancy and addressed their queries. The primary goal of the meetings was to enhance parents' awareness regarding vaccination while dispelling misconceptions about vaccines. The two events involved 73 parents who had initially refused vaccination.

5) To support Azerbaijan’s government in promoting routine childhood vaccination, various educational materials were developed:
1. Questions & Answers Brochure: Addresses key questions and dispels vaccine myths. Printed and distributed during European Immunization Week and other vaccine-related events, with 197,750 copies.
2. Brochure on Vaccine-Preventable Diseases: Provides fundamental vaccine information. 7,750 copies delivered, more to be distributed after approval of the new national immunization calendar.
3. Measles Poster and Flyer: 5,300 posters distributed to vaccine facilities via TABIB at immunization events. Additionally, 203,000 flyers printed and are being distributed during awareness events.
4. Rubella Poster and Flyer: 5,300 posters distributed via TABIB at immunization events. Furthermore, 203,000 flyers printed and are being disseminated during events.
5. Vaccine Puzzle: Entertaining and educational material for kids. 600 pieces printed and disseminated to  caregivers during awareness-raising events.

Aim: to provide evidence-based information, to raise awareness
Stakeholders: MoH, TABIB, SAMHI
Main beneficaries: Caregivers, vaccine-hesitant families.

Moving forward, the plan was to prepare evidence-based recommendations on changes in medical education curricula to help Azerbaijan's public health professionals to develop competencies defined by international standards. The action is funded by USAID and implemented by WHO in collaboration with the Ministry of Health, the State Agency for Mandatory Health Insurance and TABIB.

2) WHO Azerbaijan hosted a workshop with experts from health education and health provider institutions, to develop small-scale COPC intervention plans in Nasimi district. The goal was to improve health outcomes in the District via collaboration between healthcare providers and the community while considering population characteristics and prioritizing health problems. On the first day, participants visited the District's health centers to observe and collect data on the population’s health and identify common health issues. For the remaining days, they worked on community characterization, prioritization of health issues, and a detailed assessment of health problems. The working groups then developed a comprehensive COPC intervention plans for the District. This workshop was organized under the public health focus areas of the APR funded by USAID and implemented by WHO in collaboration with the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Azerbaijan, the SAMHI, TABIB, and supported by Nasimi District Executive Power of Baku.

The seminar was attended by members of the "Capacity Group on Public Health" representing MoH, TABIB and SAMHI, teachers of the Faculty of Public Health of Azerbaijan Medical University, and WHO experts. Discussions were held on the individual learning plans presented at the seminar and the gaps between international standards and local competencies identified in the evaluations. The outcome of the seminar is that Participants have become familiar with the ASPHER competency framework, which identified their learning needs and developed time-bound individual learning plans with the support of WHO experts. The long-term aim is to prepare evidence-based recommendations on changes in medical education curricula to help Azerbaijan's public health professionals develop competencies defined by international standards.

projects.name: 2.2.1.14 - Application of the Degree of Urbanisation (DEGURBA) for the Production of Comparable Urban Data in Azerbaijan
projects.description:
Project background
With the adoption of the sustainable development goals (SDGs) in 2015 and the New Urban Agenda (NUA) in 2016 - both of which seek to track performance at the city level, there was a recognized and urgent need to work more actively towards harmonization of how cities, urban and rural areas are defined. To work towards this goal, a voluntary commitment was established in 2016, under whose umbrella UN-Habitat, the European Commission, FAO, OECD, and the World Bank have undertaken several activities to create a globally harmonized and agreeable approach that can be applied uniformly in the production of comparable data for the SDGs and NUA indicators. These efforts have sought after a method that complements, rather than replaces existing national definitions, and one that would be easily applicable across contexts. One of the activities implemented by UN-Habitat and the European Commission with partners between 2018 and 2019 was a project titled “Assessing the feasibility of applying a global definition of cities/urban areas in support of global monitoring of SDGs and NUA urban targets”, through which the recommended harmonized approach – the Degree of Urbanization concept (DEGURBA) was introduced during the 51st UN Statistical Commission meeting (March 2020) endorsed DEGURBA as a sound approach to defining urban and rural areas for statistical comparisons.

The strategy for implementing the pilot project involves a series of country specific trainings, during which policy makers as well as technical teams from the statistical offices, mapping agencies, urban authorities, learning and research institutions and other relevant local partners are introduced to the concepts and technical details of DEGURBA, its implementation workflow, and how the boundaries resulting from its application are applied in the computation of SDG 11 indicators.

During the consultative sessions, Member States, upon acknowledgement of the value added for DEGURBA strongly indicated the need for country-specific capacity building and more engagement with policy makers on the approach, and how it can be implemented using locally produced data. These sentiments were further echoed during the Statistical Commission meeting, with specific requests to the proponents of the approach to work with Member States to test the approach, and to develop relevant technical material for the methodology implementation. 

To respond to the requests from Member States during the consultative workshops and the recommendations from the statistical commission, UN-Habitat and the European Commission, in coordination with other partners involved in the urban-rural areas definitions harmonization process developed the project titled “Application of the DEGURBA approach to generate comparable urban data in selected countries”. The project, which is being implemented in 13 countries between September 2021 and June 2023 has a goal of strengthening the capacity of national governments to adopt and integrate the DEGURBA approach into their data management structures.

The strategy for implementing the pilot project involves a series of country specific trainings, during which policy makers as well as technical teams from the statistical offices, mapping agencies, urban authorities, learning and research institutions and other relevant local partners are introduced to the concepts and technical details of DEGURBA, its implementation workflow, and how the boundaries resulting from its application are applied in the computation of SDG 11 indicators. Working with these stakeholders, National Statistical Offices are expected to use the DEGURBA approach to generate disaggregated data that is critical for policy formulation and decision making, as well as to facilitate their annual reporting on the urban SDGs.

Output 2.1.2 - National primary health care and nutrition systems are strengthened to ensure universal coverage and quality, inclusive and high-impact interventions
Output 2.1.3 - Providers of public and social protection services have improved capacity to target the most vulnerable groups with quality, effective and innovative solutions
Output 2.1.4 - National policies and mechanisms are strengthened to promote and protect human rights, increase access to justice and participatory mechanisms, and sustain social cohesion

Output 2.1.5 - Institutional capacities are enhanced to effectively develop and implement governance programmes, public service delivery, youth engagement and modernization of services to bridge the digital divide
Outcome 2.2 - Quality, disaggregated and timely data is available and used to inform decision-making and policies that leave no one behind
Output 2.2.1 - Institutional capacities are strengthened to improve monitoring and reporting on the SDGs and on furthest behind persons
Output 2.2.2 - National capacities are enhanced to generate evidence-based policies and decisions

framework.name: Strategic Priority 3 - Protecting the environment & addressing climate change

children.name: Outcome 3.1 - People including those left behind benefit from climate strategies and environment protection policies that ensure natural resources are sustainably managed, livelihoods are protected, and resilience strengthened
Output 3.1.1 - Institutional capacities to plan, track and report on climate change, and to access climate finance and technologies, are strengthened
Output 3.1.2 - Adaptive policies on land use, integration to the tourism value chain and water management are set up to enhance the resilience of vulnerable communities
Output 3.1.3 - Energy policies and solutions reduce emissions and save energy
Output 3.1.4 - Evidence-based policies, mechanisms and practices are adopted to reduce environmental hazards and pollution in urban and rural areas

framework.name: Strategic Priority 4 - A gender-equitable society that empowers women and girls

children.name: Outcome 4.1 - Women and girls, including those furthest behind, benefit from enhanced national mechanisms that ensure they are protected from discrimination and violence and empowered to participate in all spheres of life
Output 4.1.1 - Costed action plans on gender equality are set up and implemented
Output 4.1.2 - Stereotypes of women and girls are reduced in public discourse
Output 4.1.3 - Women and girls have skills and knowledge to enjoy equal rights and opportunities
